title.narrative: Provide vulnerable women and girls, including GBV survivors and persons living with disabilities, access to quality, safe, timely and confidential GBV services in rural Jowhar Rural - Middle Shabelle.

description.narrative:
ltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Calibri, sans-serif border-color: windowtext"gtThe proposed project by IRDO will be implemented in rural Jowhar for a period of 10 months. Vulnerable women and girls, including GBV survivors and persons living with disabilities will be provided with quality access, safe, timely and confidential GBV services. lt/spangtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtTo ensure referral based on need in accordance with the area-based service mapping and standard operating procedures (SOPs) created by the GBV AoR, and to support access to CMR service providers (trained on CMR protocols), IRDO will provide GBV specialized services through trained case management teams. These will be administered by specialized teams of case workers, PSS, and supervisors. A total of 100 project participants will be targeted in this initiative. IRDO will provide unconditional cash voucher assistance inform of cash to support vulnerable and poor families' negative coping strategies like early/forced marriage to leverage social and financial security or risk of sex in exchange for food so as to prevent further vulnerability attributed to low economic status. The cash voucher assistance will be administered for a period of 5 months upon which 500 project participants will have access to cash so as to improve on their protection and reduce exposure to sexual exploitation, harassment and GBV cases. lt/spangtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Calibri, sans-serif border-color: windowtext"gtIn accordance with the GBV AoR guidelines, IRDO will purchase and provide GBV products, such as dignity kits, to 1036 GBV survivors and vulnerable women and girls in the target areas of rural Jowhar. lt/spangtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtAccording to assessment reports, shocks like climate-induced drought, man-made conflicts (war and displacement), and communities devastated by flooding heighten women's susceptibility, posing a risk to their safety. In order to retain their human dignity, GBV survivors, weak women, and girls who cannot afford basic hygiene products will receive dignity kits from IRDO. Dress (Dirac), Shawl (Garbasar), Sanitary Cloth, Panties (Different Sizes), Bar Soap (250 gm), Pack of Power Soap (100 gm), Petticoats (Gorgorat), and Head Scarves (Shash) are among the products that will be delivered. During humanitarian situations, dignity kits assist women and girls in maintaining their dignity. The ability to preserve self-worth and confidence is crucial for navigating challenging and potentially overwhelming humanitarian situations. Boosting women's self-confidence and self-esteem helps them feel more capable of caring for and protecting their children. As guided by a proper diagnosis in consultations with organizations of persons with disabilities, IRDO will procure and distribute mobility aid to GBV survivors who are living with disabilities. This will incorporate Elbow/Auxiliary crutches and where possible wheel chairs. In addition to providing survivors and at-risk women and girls with age- and culturally-appropriate psychosocial one-on-one and group counseling and support, IRDO will also connect them to other service providers based on their needs through the created one-stop center. The OSC or WGSS strives to foster trust between the vulnerable women and girls and project teams made up of community mobilizers who inform participants about the OSC's services, counselors, case workers, and supervisors when needed. Lastly, IRDO will carry out community mobilization and awareness on GBV, SEA and FGM mitigation and available services in the target areas of operation. The intention is to inform the community on the availability of services and how to access them.lt/spangt
